The Brooks House study, if the special town meeting approves it, could lead toward a future vote on selling or leasing a town-owned property.

The facility cost overruns on 911 cabling, the generator and the fire alarm mean the capital plan may need more money than was budgeted, a gap the committee discussed covering with leftover ARPA funds.

All high school students pay a mandatory annual activity fee funding guest speakers, advisor stipends, Science Olympiad, graduation/homecoming supplies and some field trip bus costs; students who don't pay cannot graduate. The board discussed whether it is fair as a mandatory, non-optional fee.
Middle school clubs such as ski club and Science Olympiad charge a per-club fee covering supplies, registration and some transportation.
Turkey Hill charges a fee for after-school activities, funding teacher stipends and materials for a roughly five-week session.
The primary school charges a similar fee for its after-school activity sessions, funding stipends and materials.

The committee discussed returning ARPA funds to the town for reappropriation by the select board, consistent with what was represented at town meeting, and asked to be part of future discussions on how the money is reused.

meetings.headline: Override passed, giving Lunenburg schools level-service funding but no expansion as ESSER funds end
meetings.summary: This School Committee meeting was largely a post-override celebration and reporting session: public comment and the chair's report thanked voters, staff, and advocates for the town's successful override vote, which will level-fund schools (offsetting expiring ESSER money) without expanding programs. The committee voted to reject a proposed rainwater retention/stormwater demonstration project at the middle-high school after learning it was sited without consulting the district and had already cost several thousand dollars in engineering, and voted not to increase school choice seats to protect small class sizes; it also received presentations on a new family-school partnership compact, the state's new IEP form, and facilities project updates.

budget_items.what_was_said: The chair reported a legislative bill sponsored by MASC, MASS, MTA and AFT that would apply an inflation adjustment to Chapter 70; a MASC representative told her it would bring Lunenburg new funding if passed.

The chair said the town is not a held-harmless community; it got a small percentage increase last year after its low-income count rose, which is more than held-harmless towns get but far less than other communities receive.

A committee member asked how much was spent designing the stormwater BMP without consulting the school district first; the presenter estimated the range for the engineering design work.
The chair said a legislator has been pushing for an earmark tied to enhanced 911 funding for the town that could come through now that the override passed.

A speaker thanked everyone who participated in the town vote on the override.
